Implement this by making the grad-accumulation step count a function of training progress (time fraction). Keep LR schedules unchanged. The aim is more updates early, when gradient noise is low relative to the signal.

backlog.spec: After Muon's orthogonalization step, apply a per-row (output neuron) adaptive normalization. Keep an EMA (beta 0.95) of the mean squared value of each row of the orthogonalized update. Divide each row by the square root of its EMA plus 1e-8. Then rescale the whole update so its Frobenius norm matches the pre-normalization norm. Apply to all matrix params. Keep the existing LR and weight decay.

Disable it at eval. Skipped layers save compute, which should give slightly more steps in the time budget. Make sure torch.compile does not recompile, for example by drawing the mask as a tensor multiplier instead of using Python control flow.
backlog.title: Stochastic depth (layer drop) ramp

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss predicting the token 2 positions ahead from the final hidden state. Use a small extra linear head (n_embd to vocab) or reuse lm_head after a lightweight learned projection of the final hidden state. Weight its cross-entropy at 0.3 and linearly anneal the weight to 0 over the warmdown. The reported and evaluated loss path must remain the standard next-token head only. Do not touch the evaluation call.

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of all model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every step in fp32 on GPU). After training finishes and before the final evaluation call, copy the EMA weights into the model. Do not change the evaluation function. backlog.spec: For the first 30% of the time budget train on sequences cropped to 512 tokens. Do this by reshaping each batch into 4x as many rows of length 512 with the same token count. Then use the full length for the rest. Short sequences cost less attention compute and give more steps early. Handle the sliding window sizes and the rotary cache so that they work at both lengths. Accept the one extra torch.compile recompile.

backlog.spec: Change the MLP to a gated form: out = proj(relu(gate(x))^2 * up(x)). Set the hidden size to about 8/3*n_embd, rounded to a multiple of 128, so the parameter count stays near the baseline's 4x ReLU^2 MLP. Initialize proj to zero as before, and put gate and up under Muon with the other matrices.

backlog.spec: Add value residual: keep the first layer's attention value tensor v1. In every later layer, mix the layer's value as v = (1-a)*v + a*v1, with a learnable scalar a per layer, initialized at 0.5 and trained under the scalar Adam group. Apply this to layers that do not already use value embeddings, or blend it on top of them if they do. Keep the shapes consistent with GQA and heads.

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so accumulation steps are halved). In a 300 s budget, twice as many optimizer steps usually helps a small model. Leave all LRs unchanged; make sure any code deriving grad_accum_steps from TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE still works.

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated every optimizer step with torch._foreach_lerp_ under no_grad. memo:
Incumbent is now 1.0960 (slot 10), from halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18. That was the only accepted change and by far the biggest gain (-0.0185). More optimizer steps in the 300 s budget matter most.

The batch change moved the baseline, so the earlier single-run deltas are not comparable to it. Against the new incumbent:
- UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.008 scored 1.0874/1.0899 (-0.0074). It was rejected, but it looks promising and is worth re-testing.
- EMA scored 1.0900/1.0927 (-0.0047), also rejected.
- Stacking init and beta2 scored 1.0941 (-0.0019).
- WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 was worse (+0.0027).

Try next:
1. Go smaller on batch (2**17).
2. Combine UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.008 with EMA.
3. Re-test the init and beta2 changes on the new baseline.

Leave MATRIX_LR, weight decay and the MLP alone.
